evidence.snippet: Hydrolethalus Syndrome (HLS) is a severe autosomal recessive ciliopathy characterized by developmental defects (polydactyly, hydrocephaly, and cleft lip or palate) that lead to lethality around birth.

nodes.description: HYLS1 anchors the centriole at the apical membrane and is required for transition fibre formation, transition zone organization and the ciliary gate that controls entry of intraflagellar transport particles. Loss of these functions reduces primary cilia in some tissues (for example the kidney in knock-in mice) but not others.

evidence.reference_title: The hydrolethalus syndrome protein HYLS-1 links core centriole structure to cilia formation.
evidence.snippet: A single amino acid change in human HYLS1 leads to a perinatal lethal disorder termed hydrolethalus syndrome, and we show that this mutation impairs HYLS-1 function in ciliogenesis.

evidence.reference_title: The hydrolethalus syndrome protein HYLS-1 regulates formation of the ciliary gate.
evidence.snippet: Loss of HYLS-1 compromises the docking and entry of intraflagellar transport (IFT) particles, ciliary gating for both membrane and soluble proteins, and axoneme assembly.

nodes.description: In mammalian cells HYLS1 binds and activates the ciliary lipid kinase PIPKIgamma, allowing axoneme nucleation and assembly of the NPHP module. Without it, beta-arrestin cannot leave the cilium, GPR161 is not removed, and Hedgehog signaling cannot be activated. HYLS1 D211G still supports ciliogenesis in these cells but not Hedgehog activation.

evidence.reference_title: Ciliopathy protein HYLS1 coordinates the biogenesis and signaling of primary cilia by activating the ciliary lipid kinase PIPKIγ.
evidence.snippet: HYLS1 deficiency interrupts the assembly of ciliary NPHP module and agonist-induced ciliary exit of β-arrestin, which, in turn, disturbs the removal of ciliary Gpr161 and activation of hedgehog (Hh) signaling.

nodes.description: Ciliary signaling failure during organogenesis is thought to derail patterning of the forebrain midline, skull base, face, limbs and lungs, producing the fixed malformation pattern of the syndrome. The link from the cellular defects to each malformation is inferred from ciliopathy biology and the knock-in mouse; it has not been traced organ by organ in patients. Fetal tissue also shows an immature, disorganized cortex with abnormal radial glia, and neuronal progenitors from patients cycle faster and undergo less apoptosis.

nodes.description: CEP120 recruits HYLS1 to the centriole, where HYLS1 recruits inner scaffold proteins that stabilize the centriolar microtubule wall. D211G weakens the CEP120 interaction, so HYLS1 is displaced and the distal end of the centriole degenerates, giving short or broken centrioles in a tissue-specific way.
